notes.note: Ambiguous; chose reading 1: a template with ifpresent on the template as a whole used directly in a receive operation is an error. Titan accepts it (does not implement restriction b).

Ambiguous and hard to test: the spec examples themselves allow spaces after commas in \q{...} and #(n, m), and invalid metacharacters keep their literal value (B.1.5.0-051a). Chose whitespace inside a reference metacharacter "{ c_ref }" as the violation. Titan accepts it.
Ambiguous; chose reading that \q{U0171, U0041} matches the sequence of the listed characters (consistent with char(U..., U...) in 6.1.1).
Titan rejects {\c_ref} ("Invalid reference expression"); the syntax is explicitly defined in Table B.1 and B.1.5.2 EXAMPLE 1, so Titan does not support it.
Covers TAB, LF, VT, FF, CR and SP only; the ISO/IEC 10646 clause 17.2 space characters (universal charstring) are not checked.
Only checks a boundary between a graphical character and SP, and absence of a boundary between two letters; boundaries at string start/end are not covered as their semantics is unclear.
Observes root-type matching by assigning the subtype template to a charstring template variable and matching "xyz", which is outside the subtype.
Titan rejects lone '#' and ']' in patterns; per B.1.5.0 such metacharacter symbols not forming a valid metacharacter retain their literal value, so the test is kept.
Informative note; tested by instantiating at runtime a pattern from a variable containing stray metacharacter symbols and expecting literal matching instead of an error.
Informative note; tested with \N{v_char} referencing a variable of length 2, which B.1.5.4 requires to produce an error (expected at runtime).
Follows EXAMPLE 4 of B.1.5.0 (pattern referencing a template containing ?), which the standard states is an error. Titan accepts it (check not implemented).
